evidence: Variant deck build/recovery/tmp-decks/deck1-hooks.json (entity release, both flag trials, controls pass, no lost passing measurements): baseline release passes bytes on both trials but fails references with missing_absolute_relocations [23]; all three hook-global candidates emit relocation offset 23 -> ?WaveDeviceDestroyHook@@3P6AXXZA with per-relocation result unknown and an instruction stream decoded identical to baseline (a1 ........ at offset 22, the two consecutive `mov [esi+0x14], 0` stores at offsets 33/40 preserved, 51 bytes).

Post-edit `recover tasks check wave-device-control-recovery`: function results move from 32 pass / 11 fail / 4 unknown to 34 pass / 7 fail / 6 unknown; release and delete_device are the fail->unknown movers and no previously passing measurement was lost.

Image disassembly of release 0x004C4F80-0x004C4FB3, delete_device 0x004C4F10-0x004C4F37 and create_device 0x004C4ED0-0x004C4F07: each hook load is an A1/8B absolute-memory instruction on 0x0090DB34 or 0x0090DB38, the same instruction class the comparator's absolute-relocation check covers.
payload.hypothesis: The factory/destroy hook slots at 0x0090DB34/0x0090DB38 are real address-bound globals rather than raw fixed-address reads: the image's hook loads (`mov eax, dword ptr [0x90db38]` at 0x004C4FA6 in release, the matching forms in create_device/delete_device) carry absolute relocations, which a `*reinterpret_cast<T**>(0xADDR)` inline accessor cannot emit - it compiles the same bytes with no relocation, and that missing relocation at offset 23 was the round's only failing reference. Spelling the slots as a header extern plus a TU definition carrying `// 0x0090DB34`/`// 0x0090DB38` binding comments (the established WaveDeviceGlobal 0x0090D978 / WaveDeviceReleaseGuard 0x0090DB7C treatment) emits the identical instruction WITH its relocation. The reference then verifies as unknown, not pass: the shipped image has no symbol on those dwords so link selection is unprovable - the same ceiling every code reference to process data has in this comparator (only CRT imports, verified by symbol identity, and generated-table entries verify as pass). Release and delete_device both move fail->unknown, resolving the failing obligation without regressing anything.
